Demolished BM58+ rivals by nearly 4 lengths carrying 60.5kg two starts back, then ran an excellent 2nd in the Kimberley Cup carrying 59.5kg. Drops sharply in weight down to a feather 55.5kg (122 lbs) which provides a massive physical edge over the 2200m marathon journey.

all_contenders.name: Manavendra
all_contenders.reason: Dominant winner of the Port Hedland Cup over this exact 2200m distance on August 2, powering away by 6 lengths after finishing runner-up in the Roebourne Cup. Proven dirt stamina specialist who enters in peak physical condition.

all_contenders.name: Kings Sicario
all_contenders.reason: In blistering form chasing a hat-trick of regional Cups. Won the Derby Cup over 1800m before upsetting them in the Kimberley Cup at this track over 2050m. Drops down to just 54kg (119 lbs) and has the cruising speed to handle the 2200m trip.

all_contenders.name: Maxxi Bon
all_contenders.reason: Fascinating shipper from Darwin who ran an honest 5th in the prestigious 154k Darwin Cup on August 3 after scoring over 2050m two starts back. Drawn the coveted rail barrier (stall 1) to save all the ground against the fence. | 🔻 Class Drop

all_contenders.name: Zadar Rock
all_contenders.reason: Tough North-West dirt stayer who won the Roebourne Cup and finished 2nd in the Port Hedland Cup under a crushing 63kg. Highly reliable at this distance, though conceding weight all round carrying 60.5kg (133 lbs).

all_contenders.name: Ichiban
all_contenders.reason: Solid Darwin performer who brings genuine stamina and middle-distance consistency. Well treated on 56kg and draws an ideal middle stall to track the leading division.

contenders.handicapper_notes: In blistering form this Kimberley winter season with two dominant sprint victories followed by an agonizingly close 2nd over 1700m on August 1 behind Alotta Dane. Robert Gulberti and Austin Galati are firing at this meeting. Despite drawing gate 8, his tactical cruising speed allows him to slot into a prime stalking position just off the lead. Rates as the clear top pick.

Proven Broome dirt warrior who produced a gritty 1600m victory here on July 24 defeating Magnaburma before running a solid 4th behind Alotta Dane over 1700m. Carries 131lbs but Kyra Yuill knows him intimately and will have him prominent throughout.

Massive pace threat from barrier 1. Already a dual winner at Broome this preparation leading all the way over 1700m and 2000m. Forgive her unplaced effort in Open class last start; she drops back to BM58+ handicap grade and gets ideal rail-hugging positioning to exploit the severe Broome dirt leader bias.

Rock-solid local form lines having hit the board in his last two outings behind Lucky Landing and What's The Point. Gets the benefit of barrier 3 and carries a featherweight 122lbs with Peter Farrell aboard, putting him right in the trifecta mix.

Brings strong city and provincial form from Ascot earlier in the year. Although she finished 5th over sprint trips recently, she has placed twice at this track and is well drawn in barrier 4 to appreciate stepping up to 1600m.

Possesses genuine gate speed and was only narrowly beaten over this track and trip on June 28 behind Lova Session. Tiana Murray claim offers relief from 129lbs, though the wide stall means he will have to work hard early to clear runners.
